name: PinguinoHost
desc: Runs the four Pinguino bots without Streamer.bot: Twitch chat, events, OBS, overlays. Setup page included.

help.title: AI key
help.summary: Lets ChattyPinguino and PinguinoHelper write replies.
steps: Open the Anthropic console and create an API key.
Paste it into Set here. It is never shown again.

help.title: Streamer token
help.summary: Used to read chat and events.
steps: Normally set by Sign in as streamer on the Host page; you do not paste it.
To redo, sign in again.

help.title: OBS password
help.summary: The password set in OBS under Tools > WebSocket Server Settings.
steps: In OBS enable the WebSocket server and set a password.
Paste the same password here.

help.title: PinguinoB0t token
help.summary: Lets PinguinoB0t speak as its own account.
steps: Set by Sign in on the PinguinoB0t card (private window, logged in as the bot).

help.title: ChattyPinguino token
help.summary: Lets ChattyPinguino speak as its own account.
steps: Set by Sign in on the ChattyPinguino card (private window, logged in as the bot).

help.title: PinguinoHelper token
help.summary: Lets PinguinoHelper speak as its own account.
steps: Set by Sign in on the PinguinoHelper card (private window, logged in as the bot).

_module.title: How PinguinoHost works
_module.summary: PinguinoHost runs the four chat bots, Twitch events, OBS control and Actions & Events without Streamer.bot.
steps: Sign in the streamer account once on the Host page (Sign in as streamer). This lets the Host read chat and events.
Give each bot its own Twitch account: press Sign in on its card, in a private window, logged in as that bot. Then press Send test to see which bot answers.
PinguinoB0t runs the game commands and is the fallback voice. ChattyPinguino chats and answers when @mentioned. PinguinoHelper only chimes in on key words (how to join, minecraft ip, ip, !discord).
Open Actions & Events to build commands, timers and alerts. Anything imported or preset starts disabled.
Before going live check the Pre-stream list: everything should be green. To redo any step use the item's fix button.

chat.title: Chat connection
chat.summary: The Host reads your Twitch chat with the streamer token. Green means messages are flowing in.
steps: If it is red, the streamer account is probably not signed in or the token expired.
Open the Host page, press Sign in as streamer, approve on Twitch, then wait about 10 seconds.
Check the channel name in the Host settings matches your Twitch channel.
To redo: sign in again; the old token is replaced.

eventsub.title: EventSub (follows, subs, raids, redeems)
eventsub.summary: EventSub is Twitch's live event feed. The Host subscribes to follows, subs, gifts, cheers, raids and, optionally, stream on/off and channel point redemptions.
steps: It needs the streamer signed in with all scopes. Sign in again if a subscription was refused (HTTP 403).
403 on redemptions means the token lacks channel:read:redemptions; 403 on the mod check means moderation:read. Signing in again grants both.
Optional subscriptions that are refused do not turn this red.
If the connection drops the Host retries by itself.

master.title: Master device
master.summary: Only one PC runs the bots at a time (the master) so chat never gets double answers.
steps: The Suite core decides which device is master and the Host checks every 10 seconds.
If this device is not the master the Host stays idle on purpose. Make this device the master in Devices, or run the bots on the master PC.
If the core is unreachable for 60 seconds the Host stops itself; start the Suite core, then the Host.

streamer.title: Streamer account sign-in
streamer.summary: The streamer token reads chat and events and runs timeouts and follower lookups.
steps: Open the Host page and press Sign in as streamer.
Log in on Twitch as the channel owner and approve the scopes.
The token is saved to the key vault when it is available. The pre-stream check warns before it expires.
To redo: sign in again; the new token replaces the old.

bot-core.title: PinguinoB0t account
bot-core.summary: PinguinoB0t is the main bot and the fallback voice when another bot cannot speak.
steps: On the Host page find the PinguinoB0t card and press Sign in.
Use a private window and log in as the PinguinoB0t Twitch account, not the streamer account. The page warns if the account differs.
Press Send test to confirm it speaks as itself.
If the token is about to expire, sign in again.

bot-chat.title: ChattyPinguino account
bot-chat.summary: ChattyPinguino is the chatty AI bot. It answers @mentions and the word pinguino.
steps: On the Host page find the ChattyPinguino card and press Sign in.
Use a private window and log in as the ChattyPinguino Twitch account.
Press Send test. Until it is signed in, PinguinoB0t speaks for it.
Chat also needs an AI key (see the AI key item).

bot-helper.title: PinguinoHelper account
bot-helper.summary: PinguinoHelper chimes in only on key words such as how to join, minecraft ip, ip and !discord.
steps: On the Host page find the PinguinoHelper card and press Sign in.
Use a private window and log in as the PinguinoHelper Twitch account.
Press Send test. Its facts come from innocentpenguin.com.

mod.title: PinguinoB0t is a channel mod
mod.summary: Timeouts and some moderation need PinguinoB0t to be a moderator.
steps: In Twitch chat, as the channel owner, type /mod PinguinoB0t.
If the check says it cannot check, sign the streamer in again to grant moderation:read.
If you never use timeouts you can ignore this.

modules.title: Bot modules loaded
modules.summary: The Host loads the core, chat, helper and router code from the Suite folders.
steps: Red means a file is missing or did not compile.
From the PinguinoSuite folder run node Shared/sync-shared.mjs, then restart the Host module.
Check the Console for compile errors.

obs.title: OBS connection
obs.summary: The Host controls OBS scenes, sources and reports the streaming flag over OBS WebSocket.
steps: In OBS open Tools > WebSocket Server Settings and enable the server (port 4455).
Set a password and save it in Integrations > Key vault as HOST_SECRETS.ObsPassword.
OBS must be running. The Host reconnects by itself.

streamerbot.title: Streamer.bot (legacy engine)
streamerbot.summary: Streamer.bot is no longer needed. It only matters if you still run the old setup.
steps: Yellow is fine once you moved to the Host.
If you keep both, do not enable the same command in both or chat gets double answers.
To bring old commands over use Actions & Events > Import from Streamer.bot.

ai.title: AI key for chat and helper
ai.summary: ChattyPinguino and PinguinoHelper use an AI provider to write replies. The key is stored in the vault and never shown.
steps: Create a key in the Anthropic console.
Open Integrations > Key vault and Set CHAT_BOT_API_KEY.
Once it reads green, use Remove plaintext in Integrations to delete the copy in chat_settings.json.
Limits: chat 200 calls per hour, helper 100.

faq.title: Helper facts from the website
faq.summary: PinguinoHelper answers with the Minecraft IP, port and Discord link from innocentpenguin.com so they stay current.
steps: Facts load from innocentpenguin.com/api/faq (the minecraft_ip and discord entries).
Yellow means the site could not be reached and the saved helper_facts.json is used instead.
To change an answer, edit the FAQ on the website; the Host picks it up within minutes.

vault.title: Key vault
vault.summary: The vault stores API keys and tokens encrypted on this device. The Host reads them at start and every 10 minutes.
steps: Open Integrations > Key vault and use Import into vault for the Host keys.
When the check is green, Remove plaintext deletes the copies in the settings files.
Yellow with 403 means the Suite core needs a rebuild; 409 means another device is master; 503 means this OS has no key store.
Until it works the Host keeps using the plaintext files.

errors.title: Warnings and errors
errors.summary: Shows the last warning or error the Host logged.
steps: Open the Console and filter by module host.
Click a line to see what it means and how to fix it.
Green means nothing has gone wrong since the Host started.

redeem-403.title: Channel point redemptions refused (403)
redeem-403.summary: Twitch refuses the redemption subscription until the streamer token has the channel:read:redemptions scope.
steps: Open the Host page and press Sign in as streamer again.
Approve the new permissions on Twitch.
Then enable the redeem action in Actions & Events and set the reward title exactly as on Twitch.

automations.title: Actions & Events
automations.summary: Build commands, timers, alerts and OBS actions without Streamer.bot.
steps: Open Actions & Events and press New action. Add a trigger and steps.
Press Test for a dry run first; it never sends chat or changes OBS. Run for real asks first.
Presets and imports start disabled: review them and enable what you want.
Song request actions stay off until you turn them on.

streamerbot-import.title: Import from Streamer.bot
streamerbot-import.summary: Brings your old commands, rewards and triggers into Actions & Events, disabled, for review.
steps: On Actions & Events press Import from Streamer.bot and read the preview.
Press merge to add them. C# actions and unsupported items are listed as skipped.
Review each action, then enable it. No keys or prompts are read.

bots-signin.title: Bots sign-in
bots-signin.summary: Each bot chats as its own Twitch account.
steps: Use a private window for each bot so you are not logged in as the streamer.
Press Sign in on the bot's card and approve.
The Host warns if the signed-in account is not the expected one. Press Send test afterwards.
